content:
Maya: quick q — we need to finalize the rerank response shape for provenance + quota accounting. My ask: include compact per-candidate score (small int) always, and expose full_provenance only when requested or sampled. worried about two things: (1) quota units when fanout changes, (2) console spam from huge provenance blobs.

Liam: +1 on compact always. For quota we should keep billing orthogonal: charge per-candidate "score_unit" based on model tier and precision, independent of whether full_provenance is returned. sample: 1 cheap model candidate = 1 unit, high-precision model = 3 units.

Srini: re: compact score, propose we encode as signed int16 with fixed scale (score_scaled = round(score_float * 1000)). negatives allowed for logits. protobuf-friendly and small over wire. include a `score_scale` in header for decoding.

Elsa: Console UX: default hide provenance. Add a toggle per-route to show "explain" for top-N only. Also add a link to expand full JSON in a modal instead of inlining long arrays. Keeps channel clean.

Kenji: telemetry: we need deterministic sampling for provenance to correlate regressions. Suggest server-side reservoir sampling keyed by tenant+route hash so that the same tenant's requests are sampled consistently across releases. Also record `provenance_sample_version` so we can A/B.

Liam: example response shape we discussed earlier: 
```json
{
  "request_id": "r_123",
  "scores": [1234, -56, 0],               // int16 scaled by score_scale
  "score_scale": 1000,
  "candidates": ["id_a","id_b","id_c"],
  "provenance": null,                      // present only if opt-in or sampled
  "billing": {"candidate_units": [1,3,1], "total_units": 5}
}
```
This keeps the normal path compact.

Maya: question: if provenance is sampled and not returned, should `billing.total_units` reflect actual fanout or the compacted view? Ops needs accurate charge for committed capacity.

ops-bot: automatic note: billing must reflect executed model fanout (post-routing). If a candidate was dispatched to a high-tier model, it counts the higher unit even if we don't return its provenance.

Srini: agree with ops-bot. Also propose an explicit `fanout_manifest` field that is always populated but compact: `[{model:"r49-v2", units:3, count:2}]` — small and useful for billing + quick console aggregations.

Elsa: console-bot: Console can render `fanout_manifest` as stacked bar and only fetch `provenance` on expand. We'll also add a telemetry card that shows sampling rate and sample keys.

Kenji: fallback story: if a model isn't compatible with int16 quantization (e.g., needs double precision for explain) the runtime will set `score_scale: 1` and `scores` will be larger ints. We should document that and provide a `score_precision_hint` enum.

Maya: rollout UX: plan — default: compact path only. 1% global server-side provenance sampling (tenant-consistent). add route-level admin toggle to opt-in full_provenance = true for dev tenants. For canaries, set 5%.

Liam: compatibility: make sure older SDKs ignore unknown fields. `provenance` can be a stringified blob if SDKs can't parse new shape.

Srini: also add a lint rule in model onboarding that declares `unit_cost` and `precision_category` so runtime can compute `candidate_units` deterministically.

Maya: ok I'll draft the API doc and proto example. owners: Maya (API), Srini (runtime billing), Elsa (console UX), Kenji (telemetry).

Liam: sounds good. I'll add the int16 decode helper to the SDKs PR. :+1:

Elsa: I'll sketch console toggle patterns and modal for full provenance.

Maya: thanks all — will open a PR with the response examples and rollout plan by EOD.

Kenji: one last: add server-side flag `provenance_consistency_id` so we can fetch the exact sampled payload later for debugging without storing full payload inline in logs.

Maya: good call. added to notes.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled rollout job created: canary=eng-platform-dev, sample_rate=0.05, start=2024-11-05T14:00Z

Maya: noted. closing thread after PR posted.
